children: Consolidated EBITDA increased 80.40 per cent to Rs 54.30 crore from Rs 30.11 crore a year earlier

Aimtron Electronics reported an 83.32 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue from operations to Rs 224.71 crore in the first half of FY27, compared with Rs 122.58 crore in the corresponding period last year.
The electronics design and manufacturing company’s consolidated net profit rose 71.48 per cent to Rs 34.79 crore during the April-September period, against Rs 20.29 crore in H1 FY26.

Consolidated EBITDA increased 80.40 per cent to Rs 54.30 crore from Rs 30.11 crore a year earlier. However, the EBITDA margin moderated to 24.17 per cent from 24.60 per cent, while the profit after tax margin declined to 15.48 per cent from 16.55 per cent.
The company’s unexecuted consolidated order book stood at Rs 733.27 crore as of 30 September 2026, reflecting demand across telecom, power, industrial electronics and emerging technology segments.

Telecom and network security accounted for 26 per cent of the order book, followed by power at 24 per cent and Internet of Things (IoT), robotics and drones at 20 per cent. Industrial electronics contributed another 10 per cent. The remaining orders were spread across automotive and battery management systems, ruggedised electronics, battery energy storage systems, medical technology and other segments.
Domestic business accounted for 78 per cent of the order book, while exports contributed 22 per cent.
Aimtron's international subsidiary, AIC, also reported an increase in its unexecuted order book, which rose approximately 161 per cent year-on-year to USD 18.8 million.
The subsidiary has customer engagements across industrial electronics, power and energy, ruggedised electronics, IoT and robotics, medical technology, and aerospace and defence.

Commenting on the performance, Mukesh Jeram Vasani, Chairman and Managing Director of Aimtron Electronics, said the growth reflected the company's execution capabilities, operational efficiencies and increasing contribution from higher-value manufacturing and design-led solutions.
He said the company was witnessing opportunities in sectors requiring advanced electronics, integrated solutions and high-reliability manufacturing.

Aimtron is focusing on expanding its capabilities in original design manufacturing (ODM), integrated box-build solutions and system integration. It is also looking to strengthen its presence in international markets, particularly the US and Europe.

The company said it would continue investing in manufacturing infrastructure, engineering and design capabilities as it seeks to expand its global operations and execute its existing order book during the remainder of FY27.
